content.text: All preferred elements appear satisfied. Submitting a compliant finding without a redline.

input.quote: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
input.rationale: The licence package meets the preferred position in full. Section 13.1 grants the subscription/access rights to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" (with Authorized Users permitted), so affiliates and contractors are covered without any notice condition. Section 13.2 makes paid-up software and embedded Vendor Technology licences "perpetual, irrevocable" to Customer and its Affiliates, including a right to permit contractors to support the material, and Section 14.3 extends that perpetual licence to Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable. Section 13.3 limits Vendor's ability to revoke or suspend to "a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure," which is the preferred uncured-material-breach-only standard for the subscription licence. Section 13.3 also permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, and Section 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor's consent, with Section 24.2 restricting Vendor-side assignment and Section 24.4 barring termination, suspension or repricing on Customer change of control. The Section 13.4 use restrictions are narrow (reverse engineering, interference, security bypass, unlawful use) and expressly do not limit authorized testing or use of Customer Data and output, so they do not undercut the grant. No redline is warranted; the clause benefits us as drafted.
